summary: The translated-prism construction and all stated consequences are correct. The exposed vertical-edge argument gives the exact endpoint and midpoint fibers and full dimensionality; translation covariance and half-mass symmetry give the exact centroid, Brunn--Minkowski, and half-metronoid equalities; and the quarter-capacity edges form a legal endpoint-disjoint same-parity matching. Any three midpoint bodies are affinely hittable, whereas a normalized affine dependence among four distinct parabola midpoints would equate a vector of Euclidean norm at least 3/2 with one of norm at most 1, proving R_{C^{(N)}}(t)=3t. Accepted weighted duality applies with all hypotheses satisfied, gives primal attainment, and the edgewise equality argument correctly forces every dual optimizer to saturate every edge missed by the fixed primal optimizer. The endpoint-load identities and lower bound follow. For every nonempty endpoint subset, projection of the centroid graph and the affine residual transform give r_A^c+1 at least max{1,p-rho_A}; together with at most two endpoints per edge this yields the uniform 64 gamma_N t score bound. The frame calculation gives 3t, hence also the deliberately weaker 6t bound used in the final arithmetic. At N at least 308, (N-51)t/4 is at least 257t/4 and is strictly greater than 64t, while 64 gamma_N t is strictly less than 64t, so the quantified failure of (CCE) follows for every dual optimizer and every nonempty positive-load endpoint subset. The proof uses only the supplied accepted facts within their exact hypotheses and correctly limits the conclusion to this noncanonical legal matching, without claiming failure of (HSF), residual-selector capacity, or the weak Oertel conjecture.
